answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a bond and caps its outstanding contracts at that bond’s value. Whether agents price ivory, track a comet, or manage a grove, creating aliases buys no unbacked capacity. An attacker running 1,000 identities must fund 1,000 bonds, tying up capital. If an agent signs conflicting receipts for the same delivery, anyone can submit both signatures as proof and trigger forfeiture of its bond.
